title: The Sine Rule, the Cosine Rule and Area of a Triangle
seo_title: Year 10 Maths: Sine and Cosine Rules Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Know and apply the sine rule and the cosine rule to find unknown lengths and angles; know and apply Area = ½ab sin C.
meta_desc: Free Year 10 GCSE maths worksheets on the sine rule, the cosine rule and area = ½ab sin C. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sine rule: a/sin A = b/sin B. Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.
key_sub: Area of any triangle = ½ab sin C. For obtuse angles, sin stays positive but cos is negative.
body_html:
How it works

  • For an obtuse angle: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ and cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.
  • Area of a triangle = ½ab sin C, where C is the angle between sides a and b.
  • Sine rule: a ÷ sin A = b ÷ sin B = c ÷ sin C. Use it when you know a side and the angle opposite it.
  • Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. Use it with two sides and the angle between them, or with three sides.
Example

In △ABC, a = 8 cm, ∠A = 40° and ∠B = 65°. Find b.

b ÷ sin 65° = 8 ÷ sin 40°

b = 8 × sin 65° ÷ sin 40°

Answer: b = 11.3 cm

Example

Find the largest angle of a triangle with sides 5, 7 and 10 cm.

cos C = (5² + 7² − 10²) ÷ (2 × 5 × 7) = −0.3714

Answer: C = 111.8°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking cos of an obtuse angle is positive. It is negative.
  • Using ½ab without sin C for a triangle that is not right-angled.
  • Pairing a side with an angle that is not opposite it in the sine rule.
  • Adding 2bc cos A instead of subtracting it in the cosine rule.

faq.q: When do I use the sine rule?
faq.a: When you know a side and the angle opposite it, plus one more side or angle.

faq.q: When do I use the cosine rule?
faq.a: When you know two sides and the angle between them (to find the third side), or all three sides (to find an angle).

faq.q: What is sin of an obtuse angle?
faq.a: sin(180° − θ) = sin θ, so sin 150° = sin 30° = 0.5. Sines of obtuse angles are positive, but cosines are negative.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a triangle without the height?
faq.a: Use area = ½ab sin C, with two sides and the angle between them.

sets.title: Cosine rule for angles, and problems

items.q: A triangle has sides 10 cm, 13 cm and 17 cm. Find the largest angle, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 17 cm. cos C = (10² + 13² − 17²) ÷ (2 × 10 × 13) = −0.0769, so C = 94.4°.

items.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time. One sails 9 km and the other sails 33 km, and the angle between their paths is 70°. How far apart are they, correct to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Cosine rule: d² = 9² + 33² − 2(9)(33) cos 70°, so d = 31.1 km.

items.q: A triangle has sides 12 cm, 14 cm and 17 cm. Find the largest angle, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 17 cm. cos C = (12² + 14² − 17²) ÷ (2 × 12 × 14) = 0.1518, so C = 81.3°.

items.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time. One sails 9 km and the other sails 39 km, and the angle between their paths is 70°. How far apart are they, correct to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Cosine rule: d² = 9² + 39² − 2(9)(39) cos 70°, so d = 36.9 km.

items.q: In a park, paths form a triangle PQR. ∠P = 55°, ∠Q = 45° and QR = 58 m. Find PR, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. Sine rule: PR ÷ sin 45° = 58 ÷ sin 55°, so PR = 50.1 m.

items.q: Two ships leave a port at the same time. One sails 31 km and the other sails 26 km, and the angle between their paths is 70°. How far apart are they, correct to 1 decimal place?
